title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. E is an elliptic curve over k with char k ≠ 2. J = I = ₂E(k)* is the set of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. V_J(k) = Ker(k^J --sum--> k) is 2-dimensional (identified with Γ(Σ_J, O(1))), and Σ_J = P(V_J) is the 'Legendre line'. On Σ_J the three points indexed by J are the cusps, and the point t ∈ Σ_J is the Legendre (λ-) invariant of E with its 2-torsion. ω̲ is the μ_2-torsor of circular orders on J, and the twist (ω̲) makes det V_J ≅ k(ω̲) canonical. Grothendieck is building an 'épi-flag de Legendre', a rigidification of (E, ₂E) by data α = i∧ω (with i ∈ μ_4*(k), ω a circular order) and an isomorphism K: t_E ≅ O_t(1). This page states and explains the normalisation of K.

(77) K must satisfy: K^{⊗2} is the identity of T_{Σ_J,t} under two canonical isomorphisms.
- The first, t_E^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}, is the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for the Legendre family. The tangent space to the moduli at E is H^1(E,T_E) ≅ t_E ⊗ H^1(E,O_E) ≅ t_E^{⊗2} by Serre duality.
- The second is O_t(1)^{⊗2} = O_t(2) ≅ O_t(2)(ω̲) ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}. This comes from the Euler sequence T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ det V^∨, where det V_J is trivial up to the orientation torsor ω̲, trivialised via α.
- So K is a square root of the Kodaira–Spencer map at t. For fixed α it is determined up to sign. For α free it is determined up to μ_4(k), since changing i by μ_4 and ω by μ_2 combine.

(78) The tautological sequence at t: 0 → F_t → V_J(k) = Γ(O(1)) --ev_t--> O_t(1) → 0, where F_t is the sections of O(1) vanishing at t, and F_t ≅ O_t(-1)(ω̲) by det V ≅ k(ω̲).

(79) The 'principal part' sequence: 0 → k·1 → Γ(Σ_J, O{t}) → T_{Σ_J,t} → 0. Here O{t} = O(t) is functions with at most a simple pole at t, and O(t)|_t is the normal = tangent line, giving the residue/polar-part map.

(80)–(81) Claim: (79) is canonically isomorphic to (78) ⊗ F̌_t, with F̌_t ≅ O_t(1)(ω̲). The maps are:
- F_t ⊗ F̌_t = k;
- V ⊗ F̌_t → Γ(O{t}) given by s ⊗ s_0^* ↦ s/s_0, where s_0 spans F_t;
- O_t(1) ⊗ F̌_t = O_t(2)(ω̲) ≅ T_t.
Grothendieck remarks that this holds for any locally free rank-2 module V̲ with a section t of P(V̲). The point is to transport the condition on K into conditions on a family (δ_i) ∈ t_E^J. The next page uses exactly this: K ↔ Ǩ: ť_E ≅ F_t ↔ a monomorphism ť_E → V_J(k) with image F_t, and the conditions (sum zero, proportionality, Legendre normalisation).
errors: No mathematical error found. The identifications (Euler sequence twisted by the orientation torsor, residue sequence for O(t), tensoring the tautological sequence by F̌_t) are correct.
Minor: the identity O(1)^{⊗2} ≅ T_t only holds after twisting by ω̲, and is made canonical by α. Grothendieck tracks this correctly.
Global caveat (not an error on the page): on the Legendre line, Kodaira–Spencer is really Ω^1(log cusps) ≅ ω^{⊗2} on the stack with −1 automorphisms. Hence the μ_4 / sign ambiguity he records.

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism t_E^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t} (tangent to Legendre line at the λ-invariant)
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1_{X(2)}(log cusps), pointwise
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kodaira–Spencer; in modular-curve form Katz, Deligne–Rapoport, Faltings–Chai
ideas.where_published: Deformation-theoretic background is in SGA/FGA; this specific form is not published by Grothendieck as far as I know

ideas.what: Normalising an isomorphism K: t_E ≅ O_t(1) as a square root of Kodaira–Spencer, determined up to sign for fixed α and up to μ_4 in general
ideas.modern_name: Square root of the Kodaira–Spencer map / theta-characteristic-like structure on the level-2 (Legendre) modular stack; relation to weight-1 forms and Γ(4)-type rigidification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in the theory of modular forms of level 2/4 (Legendre and Jacobi theta relations); no single attribution

ideas.what: Tautological sequence 0→F_t→V→O_t(1)→0 with F_t ≅ O_t(-1)(det) and T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2)⊗det V^∨
Residue / principal-part sequence 0→k→Γ(O(t))→T_t→0 identified with the tautological sequence tensored by F̌_t (for any rank-2 V̲ with section of P(V̲))
ideas.modern_name: Identification O(t) ≅ O(1)⊗F̌_t on P^1; normal bundle of a point

missed.claim: Grothendieck's notion of an 'épi-flag de Legendre' rigidifies an elliptic curve with full level 2 structure by an orientation datum α = i∧ω (i ∈ μ_4*, ω a circular order on ₂E*) together with a square root K of Kodaira–Spencer. This gives a canonical μ_4-torsor-type refinement of the Legendre moduli. I know of no published account of the concept under this or another name, though the underlying facts (square roots of the Hodge bundle at level 2/4) are folklore.
missed.quote: ce qui, pour α fixé (deux choix), détermine K modulo signe. Pour α non fixé, K est déterminé modulo multiplication par μ_4(k).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a coordinate-free, functorial description of weight-1 / 'half Hodge bundle' structures on the Legendre stack, of possible interest for integral models in characteristic ≠2. It is probably reconstructible by specialists, so novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct, but largely standard projective-line and Kodaira–Spencer bookkeeping serving Grothendieck's private 'épi-flag de Legendre' formalism. The functorial square-root-of-KS normalisation with μ_4 ambiguity is a nice unpublished detail but would not surprise a specialist.

'en la tensorisant par Γ [?]' should be 'en la tensorisant par F̌_t', with (80) F̌_t ≅ O_t(1)(ω̲) given right after.
The parenthetical before (81) reads approximately '(comme on le voit de même lorsqu'on se donne un Module loc. libre de rang 2, V̲, et une section t de P(V̲) …)'.
'Rappelons-nous de la suite exacte canonique' is likely 'Rappelons-nous la suite exacte canonique'; '[-...-] je compare' has a struck-out word before 'je compare'.
